text:
Otaru is 41 minutes from Sapporo, and in winter the canal's 63 gas lamps come on by about four in the afternoon. That one fact decides whether you need a hotel there at all 👇

🤔 Half day or overnight? Guess first, then check our answer 👉 https://japanbystation.com/otaru-from-sapporo-half-day-or-overnight

❄️ HALF DAY (our pick, December to February)

Sapporo's sunset is about 16:00 all December. Leave after lunch, eat a seafood bowl at Sankaku Market next to the station, walk the canal and Sakaimachi street, and you're back at the water as the lamps light up. The last direct train back left Otaru at 23:08 on our sample weekday.

🌅 OVERNIGHT (our pick in summer)

In June sunset is after 19:00, so the lamps come on late. Staying means a sushi dinner without watching the clock, and Isezushi takes phone bookings up to two months ahead.

🚆 THE SEAT TRICK

Sit on the right leaving Sapporo. After Zenibako the line runs right along Ishikari Bay. Coming back, sit on the left.

🛶 THE HOT TICKET

The 40-minute night canal cruise sails from 16:30 to 18:30, ¥2,000. Tickets are online only; the counter doesn't sell them.

📅 WORTH KNOWING

The Otaru Snow Light Path runs 6–13 February 2027, the same week as the Sapporo Snow Festival.
